title: Optimize Console: recommendation card composer, diff sandboxing, and immutable apply ledger
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a cohesive UX surface in the Optimize Console that lets operators compose batching/caching recommendations into an apply recipe, preview diffs against a sandboxed replay (synthetic or sampled traffic), and publish changes to an append-only immutable ledger that supports safe staged rollouts and audited rollback. The goal is to enable confident, low-risk cost tuning by exposing impact estimates, test replays, and tamper-evident apply history without requiring infra engineers to manually stitch diffs together.
user_stories: As an SRE, I want to group multiple recommendations into a single apply recipe so I can roll out coordinated batching and cache settings atomically.
As a PM, I want to preview the cost and latency impact of an apply using a sandboxed replay so I can validate recommendations before applying them to production.
As a compliance officer, I want an immutable ledger of every applied config, who approved it, and a snapshot of the diff so I can audit changes months later.
As an engineer, I want automatic canary and staged rollout controls tied to the recipe so we can reduce blast radius when enabling aggressive batching or quantization.
As an operator, I want one-click rollback to the last known-good snapshot with an explanation of what changed and why.
As a developer, I want telemetry that links token-level cost delta and latency regressions back to the exact apply entry so troubleshooting is faster.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation composer UI lets users select, reorder, and annotate up to 12 recommendations and save as a named recipe.
Diff preview shows side-by-side config and estimated cost/latency delta using heuristic models and a replay engine with 'synthetic' and 'sampled traffic' modes.
Sandbox replay can run against a replica environment or local synthetic workload, produce a deterministic report, and persist a replay snapshot linked to the recipe.
Apply action writes an append-only ledger entry containing recipe metadata, author, approvers, diff snapshot, and replay report hash; entries are immutable and time-stamped.
Staged rollout controls (percentage ramp & time windows) are available at apply time and enforce automatic progressive promotion and automatic halt on regression thresholds.
Rollback action restores configs using the snapshot and records a compensating ledger entry with cause and operator comment.
Every ledger entry surfaces a unique audit URL and provides links to associated GitHub PRs, Figma mocks, and Confluence docs.
Telemetry events emitted for apply/rollback include recipe_id, ledger_entry_id, initial_estimate, observed_delta, and anomaly_flag for downstream analysis.
design_notes: Avoid the existing 'staged diff' nomenclature; call the UX element 'recipe composer' to signal composition not just diffing.
Use immutable ledger concept: append-only, cryptographic hash of snapshot and replay report to prevent tampering and ease forensic analysis.
Preview mode should surface both optimistic and conservative impact bands (p90/p50/p10) for cost and latency.
Provide a compact timeline view in the recipe detail that shows canary progress, observed metrics, and automated decision points.
Expose 'why this recommendation' inline with references to the Optimize model/runbook and the specific workload heuristics used.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Replay results may not match production due to sampling bias. Mitigation: label replay confidence and require higher approval for low-confidence replays.
Risk: Ledger growth and storage. Mitigation: compress snapshots, shard ledger storage, and provide retention policies by workspace.
Risk: Users misconfigure staged rollouts and cause flapping. Mitigation: provide sane defaults and guarded validation checks before enabling aggressive ramps.
Risk: Security exposure for stored snapshots. Mitigation: encrypt ledger entries at rest and restrict access via RBAC and audit logging.
Risk: Long-running replays delaying operations. Mitigation: cap replay runtime and provide asynchronous reports with notifications.
technical_notes: Replay engine will reuse existing Optimize replay infra component; add mode-specific adapters to run synthetic workloads.
Ledger entries should include SHA256(snapshot) and SHA256(replay_report) and persist the hashes along with storage pointers.
Add new telemetry schema keys: recipe_id, ledger_id, apply_duration_ms, observed_cost_delta_usd, latency_regression_ms.
Integrate apply flow with RBAC so only authorized roles can sign and publish a ledger entry when security_review_required is true.
Back-end API: POST /optimize/recipes/{id}/apply -> creates ledger entry, returns job id for staged rollout job.
ux_flow: 1) User navigates to Optimize -> Recommendations and selects several items.
2) Open 'Compose as Recipe' modal, reorder heuristics, add notes and a human-readable rationale, choose replay mode.
3) Run Replay: immediate quick estimate or full sandbox replay. Report is attached to the draft recipe.
4) Review Diff Preview: side-by-side config, impact bands, and replay confidence; request reviewers if required.
5) Apply: choose rollout strategy (instant/canary/staged), confirm approvers, and submit. Ledger entry is created.
6) Monitor: timeline shows canary metrics, auto-halt triggers, and manual rollback button that records a compensating ledger entry.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): enable for Redwood ops team on dev and preprod workspaces; limit to selected recipes (P0).
Phase 2 (early customers): opt-in for Dedicated customers with SLA addendum; provide training and runbooks.
Phase 3 (general availability): global release with retention defaults and admin controls; enable API access for automation.
metrics_to_track: Adoption: number of recipes created per workspace per week
Safety: percent of staged rollouts halted due to automated guards
Accuracy: replay confidence vs observed delta (difference between estimated and observed cost/latency)
Audit coverage: fraction of applies that have replay reports and approvers recorded
Mean time to rollback and rollback success rate
acceptance_test_plan: E2E: create recipe -> run synthetic replay -> apply to preprod -> verify ledger entry and telemetry emitted
Security: attempt to tamper with snapshot pointer and assert immutability via hash mismatch
Load: create 100 recipes and ensure ledger append latency remains within SLO
UX: user testing sessions with ops and two customers; gather qualitative feedback and iterate

notes_for_engineering: Ledger should be queryable by workspace and recipe id; implement pagination and retention TTLs configurable by admin.
Backfill plan: timeline UI should gracefully show historical entries even if older replays weren't captured; include 'replay_not_available' state.
Performance: ensure applying a recipe creates a background job for staged rollout; apply endpoint must be idempotent and return a job id.
